questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
First of all it depended on whether or not I could find the courses that resembled my mandatory courses from KU. 

But other than that I wanted to try and live in a smaller city with beautiful nature, and therefore Limerick ended up being perfect although I had never heard of the place before! And I realized I didn't know much about Ireland besides that the people should be very warm and open so overall it seemed like a perfect destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information about almost everything on the university's website, and if I couldn't find the necessary information the UL Erasmus team was very helpful and answered almost immediately.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the weeks leading up to the start of the exchange we received weekly emails containing a lot of information about social and academic stuff that was nice to know about. The Erasmus team had also planned an orientation week full of activities that I didn't get to attend but heard was really nice from everyone else. They also provided assistance with other questions throughout the exchange and planned other social activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are different types of housing on campus - some of them is ensuite and some of them are not but all apartments have a shared kitchen. In my apartment we where six people sharing one kitchen and I ended up getting a room with a private bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a shared kitchen in all apartments

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
So housing was something that I really wished I had known about before applying for exchange or at least in the beginning of the process after I got my acceptance letter... because Ireland is deep in a housing crisis which makes finding housing a bit of a hassle.

You can apply for on-campus housing but these are randomly assigned so there is no guarantee for getting a room. Out of 6 exchange students from KU only 2 got a room at first. 

I didn't get a room in the first place so I had to look for accommodation off campus but I was still on a waitlist for on-campus. (If you don't get a room as well stay on the waitlist!). That was quite difficult because the housing crisis makes accommodation both limited and expensive but not impossible. 

I ended up going to Ireland still without accommodation which was a big risk but I ended up being very lucky. A week before the semester started I got a call from UL saying a room on campus had become available. So it can pay off to stay calm in the situation even though it might be stressfull.  

So my advice: apply for on-campus but again don't expect to get a room. Therefore start looking for other places at the same time. There is also other student accommodations around campus that you can apply for and you have to apply for those pretty early. I didn't know that so I missed the deadline. 

But also don't panic - you are not alone and other students are in the same position and it will work out eventually.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing itself was nice and the reception was helpful. And even though UL was helpful with almost everything I felt very left on my own when I first didn't get a room on campus. Also housing is expensive both off- and on-campus but I had expected on-campus accommodation to be less expensive when thinking about it is meant for students and not as a business.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Overall it is an easy process but there is multiple registrations because they operate with a trial period of 3 weeks where you get to try different courses before selecting your final choice of courses. I found that very nice but it an be confusing because there is a broad selections of courses.
You can find all courses here:
https://bookofmodules.ul.ie
** note not all of them are offered each semester and may not be available for exchange students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can find much on the website and otherwise the Erasmus team was helpful with any question.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull! I also ended up registering for a course that wasn't officially offered to exchange students but I wrote to the course leader and she told me that I could join the course if I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try many different courses in the trial period to see what you think of the professor and the course. Sometimes you get surprised.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found some of the courses quite easy - especially on the theoretical level. But others where perfectly challenging and I felt like I learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to political science at KU there were a lot less people attending the lectures which made it more like what I had in high school. But it was nice since you were closer to your professors. Also the theoretical level was lower than back home and the assigned reading much less. But on the other hand there are many more assignments you have to hand in and most of them you have to write individually. I had five courses and midterms in all of them plus the final exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Policy-making in the European Union (replaced EP) 
- Comparative European Politics (replaced DAK3) 

Elective courses:
- Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict 
- Russian Politics 
- Sociology of Race and Racism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked 'Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict' and 'Sociology of Race and Racism'. Both had very skilled professors and interesting topics which also touched upon Irish examples

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is almost the same as in Denmark. Groceries and restaurants are a bit cheaper but not much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are so many options available for students at UL. All the clubs and societies are listed here:
https://ulwolves.ie

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
This was some of the best! There are so many clubs and societies so I definitely recommend joining these to meet a lot of new people and try new things. Some of the clubs also do weekend trips which is great fun and you get to meet a lot of Irish students as well as other internationals.

I enjoyed the kayak and surf club a lot and went on a weekend trip with both of the clubs which are some of my best memories from my time in Ireland.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ireland is not the biggest country which is great because then you get to see a lot of it! I went on a lot of weekend trips either through the clubs or self-planned with other exchange students and that is so nice! There are many busses going different places and otherwise you can rent a car and go on adventures. 

I also travelled around in Ireland for two weeks before the semester started and that was really nice. That way I got a taste of the country before everything really started. Also because there are so many things happening during the semester so there is not enough time to see everything. At least there wasn't for me.

But go and hike, and surf and stroll around in the cute cities. I recommend Dingle, Killarney, Connemara, Galway, Achill, Slieve Liegh, Aran Islands, Wicklow, Westport.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Personally I think Ireland's culture is not so far away from Danish culture so I didn't find it difficult at all. And of course there are some differences but nothing I found difficult. Irish people are very open and chatty and I think that was a very positive cultural difference:D

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies! It is a great way to connect with other students. And also the orientation week seemed really nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The Irish people's openness and that they were always so helpfull. I am definitely also gonna miss the pubs so much!! Their pub culture is like nowhere else with pints, live music, dance and great vibes. 

And then also their amazing nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Go and explore Ireland - they have much to offer from cozy small towns and pubs to beautiful mountains and hiking places 2) join clubs or societies - a great way of meeting people and enjoy the campus and Limerick 3) remember to enjoy yourself during a week of school - you can study in Limerick city to make it more cozy and celebrate in one of the many pubs of the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember the advices on housing - otherwise have fun and enjoy your time. Time goes by so quickly

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The nature and experiences with that and the people you meet<3 

I enjoyed every moment I had exploring Ireland but I enjoyed it even more because of the people I shared it with. It is really a unique experience to meet so many new people from different places of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Of course moving away from home can always be a bit challenging in the beginning especially but you figure things out along the way and that is also nice to know. I felt more confident in myself which is something I take back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
